revenge.description: If anyone attacks the ogre by surprise, be it through a sneak attack, a misfire or an unannounced ally zone attack, the ogre's rage activates and they must attack them back at least once. Everyone except the responsible becomes practically invisible for the ogre's tunnel vision until the former is hit.

small.description: Gremlins can't use great weapons. Versatile weapons are two-handed to them.

unurban.description: Can't find their way around towns, even with a map. (in-game map absent)

imposed_element_earth.description: All trolls are earthbenders by default, in addition to another element.

big_bellied.description: Everything in a troll's anatomy makes them heavier. [b]+{weight_mod}[/b] Weight Value.

homely.description: Troll faces aren't particularly attractive, which can cost them some social opportunities. Even among trolls, it's mostly the rocky shell that does the attracting.

imposed_element_air.description: All jinn are airbenders by default, in addition to another element.

imposed_element_fire.description: All tieflings are firebenders by default, in addition to another element.

short_breath.description: A tiefling's burning metabolism requires a lot of air. Disadvantage on suffocation resistance rolls.

bland_face.description: Doppler faces are remarkably similar to one another. Neither ugly nor pretty, even family and long-time friends can find it hard to recognize their true face.

squishy.description: Fairies have about as much HP as a potato chip. [b]Total HP*0.75 (rounded up)[/b].

very_small.description: One handed weapons count as great weapons to fairies. Anything else is like trying to wield a tree.

overpriced.description: Can't wear non-giant armor. Custom armor prices are tripled.[b]Tripled food need.[/b]

clumsy.description: A giant's massive frame is a huge target that takes too long to accelerate, rendering them completely unable to dodge. They suffer disadvantage to stealth and acrobatics rolls, as well as on light attack rolls.

flabby.description: Max carry weight and hand to hand damage are halved because of the soft body of a geleton.

unsightly.description: No matter how much one tries to be open minded, looking a Kaphrax in the eyes is very uncomfortable. Social encounters will be heavily affected.

compound_eyes.description: All class ability ranges are multiplied by [b]{ability_range_mult}[/b], as well as weapon range ([b]*{weapon_range_mult}[/b]).

frail.description: [b]{light_armor_bonus}%[/b], [b]{medium_armor_bonus}%[/b] and [b]{heavy_armor_bonus}%[/b] on light, medium and heavy armor values respectively.

self-conscious.description: Although they may never admit it, each failure on an active (voluntary) dice roll causes the Illithid to take [b]1d4 psychic damage[/b], [b]1d6[/b] starting at level 6, [b]1d8[/b] at level 10. This stops happening below CONST HP.

imposed_element_water.description: All thassalians are waterbenders by default, in addition to another element.

dehydrated.description: Long and short rests only bring benefits if the Thassalian is fully immersed during them. Mostly a logistics annoyance.

smelly.description: The oil produced by Thassalian skin to increase water speed does have a characteristic smell. [b]Advantage to enemy perception[/b].

nervous.description: Kemoggons are the first to react. Sometimes when they shouldn't. [b]Disadvantage[/b] to mental/physical RRs against emotion-inducing potions and spells.

many-stomached.description: These (mostly) herbivores possess very large digestive tracts which allow them to make the most out of the food they eat, which makes them heavier both with muscle and fat. [b]+{weight_mod}[/b] Weight Value.

skittish.description: Iyawana lived through experiments that recondition personality, and most of their lineages kept some deep scars from it. Iyawana have greater sensitivity to authoritative figures, suffering [b]disadvantage on social resistance rolls[/b] against them. Kings are usually heavily influential amidst Iyawana societies, recognizable as such with symbols of status they hoard and display. This behavior gave birth to the idea of the King of the Rats, a very powerful figure amongst a small community. An obviously more powerful character is also considered authoritative.

restless.description: Iyawana are stressed sleepers, who never truly rest for long. [b]A long rest is considered a short one[/b], both narratively and mechanically.

voracity.description: A meal that isn't mainly made of meat is akin to eating mud nutritionally.

ruthless.description: If not stopped, a Kenshar's instinct would push them into killing their target, even if they need them alive. To escape this yourself, surrender before they see you becoming too weak (midlife).

ham-handed.description: Kenshars, despite their best efforts, cannot write, and worse, [b]cannot draw magic circles and runes[/b].

vanity.description: An Asvyn's attire must reflect their wealth. If they don't buy a new outfit costing at least a third of their savings when arriving in a new town, OR each month living in a town, they drastically lose confidence. This results in [b]-5 Charisma[/b] and [b]disadvantage on all social rolls[/b].

cold_blooded.description: Fire and frost damage deals [b]one extra dX of double lower rank per attack stamina[/b]. For example, 1d8 twice lowered is 1d4.

apathetic.description: Cannot have emotional short and long term objectives like vengeance.
